text: Neighbourly. A smarter, safer and greener City of Elmina.
City of Elmina is home to thousands of families. But a growing township brings everyday frustrations.
When a streetlight breaks or a pothole appears, residents complain in scattered chat groups and phone calls. Nobody knows if it's being fixed, and management never sees the full picture.
Malaysia throws away around seventeen thousand tonnes of food every day, while good surplus from homes and shops ends up in the bin.
Booking the community hall still means phone calls and paper forms. Neighbours rarely know each other, and open chat groups expose phone numbers to strangers.
And living next to green forest means monkeys and snakes, with warnings that often arrive too late.
Meet Neighbourly: one private app for verified residents, local shops and Township Management.
TownCare turns complaints into tracked reports. EcoFood rescues surplus food. Residents book facilities in seconds, join community events, and find every place on one map.
An assistant answers questions in English and Malay, and a live dashboard gives Township Management the data to act.
And privacy comes first. Neighbours see Resident in Block C, never your name, number or address, unless you choose to share it.
Here's the app. It follows Sime Darby Property's colours: heritage red and warm yellow, on clean, neutral greys.

text: On a computer, everything sits in one sidebar. On a phone, the five things residents use most are in the bottom bar.
Home is deliberately calm: today's weather, the newest safety alert, what needs your attention, and what's coming up next.
Ali spots a pothole. In TownCare he adds a photo, picks a category and drops a pin on the map. Hidden location data is removed from the photo automatically.

text: His report stays anonymous to neighbours, and he can follow it in My reports and on the township map.
Township Management sees it straight away, assigns the Roads and Drainage team, and marks it resolved. Ali is notified at every step.
spoken: Township Management sees it straight away, assigns the Roads and Drainage team, and marks it resolved. Alee is notified at every step.

text: With EcoFood, neighbours and local shops share surplus food. Daniel confirms a request, and both of them see a four digit pickup code, so nobody has to swap phone numbers.
Booking a facility takes seconds. Free slots are clear, but nobody can see who booked the others.
In Community, residents filter the feed by topic, say they're going to events, and meet neighbours who chose to be listed.
The Places map pins every facility and verified local shop, with directions one tap away.
The assistant explains any feature step by step, and politely declines anything that isn't about Neighbourly.
For Township Management, the dashboard turns all of this into decisions: open reports, time to fix, wildlife sightings and food saved, each with a table view.
And everything works just as well on a phone: report a problem, share food, or ask the assistant, wherever you are.
Neighbourly. Good neighbours, verified. Helping City of Elmina become safer, greener and more connected.
